bull.b: Growth across industrial, automotive and communications reduces dependence on one market and supports durable adoption of ADI’s analog, power and signal-processing products in essential electronic systems.

High margins and substantial cash conversion provide resources for research, manufacturing capacity, acquisitions and shareholder returns, while strengthening resilience through semiconductor demand cycles.

Adding integrated voltage-regulator technology broadens ADI’s role in AI power delivery and increases its addressable market, potentially deepening customer integration and supporting multi-year growth.

bear.b: ADI serves industrial, automotive and communications customers whose capital spending can fluctuate. Prior contraction shows that strong margins and growth can weaken materially during inventory corrections or economic downturns.
Building inventory supports demand but ties up working capital and raises obsolescence risk. If growth slows, or capacity is added too early, utilization and cash returns could deteriorate.

Although ADI currently expects no material financial impact, recurring cyber incidents can create compliance costs, reputational damage, customer concerns and disruption risks across a complex global technology operation.
